newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil called 50 cts-$1 down, Brent off 5 cts.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil called 50 cts-$1 down, Brent off 5 cts.

text.p: IPE May gas oil was expected to open down 50 cents-$1 a tonne down while the June Brent contract was called only 5 cents lower as traders took a less aggressive attitude to news of recent production cuts in Nigeria, brokers said.
"We have bids already higher than (Brent) on SIMEX. Things are not as bad in Nigeria as they looked on Friday. Monday's attitude is a little more relaxed," one commented.
June Brent on SIMEX traded last off 10 cents at $18.17 a barrel but one broker said he had opening bids at $18.20 a barrel.
May gas oil closed on Friday off 75 cents at $165.25 a tonne and brokers said the contract may start weaker on Monday but recover later to retest resistance at $167.00 a tonne.
On Friday prices rose on news Shell had been forced to shut in 90,000 barrerls per day of Nigerian production but late profit-taking brought Brent back to close only one cent off the low of the day.
"Nothing has been cancelled so far so some people thought the panic was too much but we may see a rebound today," another broker said.
